title: AISC benchmark Case 1 (P-delta only), SI table, with shear deformation, P = 667

source.work: ANSI/AISC 360-22, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings (American Institute of Steel Construction), Commentary
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited page; nothing of the source is reproduced. Section properties of the W14x48 are not given by the source and are not taken from any table: I_x is calibrated on the source's own P = 0 deflection without shear deformation of Case 2, the shear flexibility on the source's P = 0 deflections with and without shear deformation (see build_problems.py and README.md)
source.location: Commentary Section C2.1, Fig. C-C2.2 (benchmark problem Case 1), SI table, column P = 667, unbracketed values

analysis: Case 1 of the source: simply supported beam-column (pin at the bottom, lateral roller at the loaded top) under a uniform transverse load of 2.92 kN/m and the axial compression P; targets: moment and deflection at midspan. Axial load level P = 667 x 1000 N (load case P holds the unit axial load, the combination factor is the level). SI table: E = 200 000 MPa, L = 8.53 m, I = 2.01011e+08 mm^4 (calibrated, see source.notes), G A_s = 2.0429e+08 N (calibrated on the P = 0 column of this case; shear deformation included: the source's unbracketed values). Member vertical along global Z, bending in the X-Z plane about local z (the section's Iz = Iy = I). Second-order analysis; the engine's member carries the exact stability functions, so one member is the exact solution of the second-order theory. The support idealisation is read from the source's sketch.

targets.precisionNote: stated tolerance 0.03 on printed "30.5" x 1000000 (unit conversion / common factor of the source); acceptance criterion stated by the source on the same page (AISC 360-22 Commentary C2.1, p. 16.1-337): moments within 3 %, deflections within 5 %; value printed to 3 significant figures
targets.sign: magnitude in the source; in the engine's convention (member local x upward, local y = global +X, loads along +X) the midspan moment Mz of Case 1 is negative and the base moment of Case 2 positive

targets.precisionNote: stated tolerance 0.05 on printed "5.84"; acceptance criterion stated by the source on the same page (AISC 360-22 Commentary C2.1, p. 16.1-337): moments within 3 %, deflections within 5 %; value printed to 3 significant figures
targets.sign: magnitude in the source; the load acts along +X, deflection +X (local y)

limitsNote: Section properties are calibrated on the source's own P = 0 values (the source gives none): the problem verifies the second-order amplification, not section properties. It does NOT test shear deformation: the source's acceptance tolerance (3 % on moments, 5 % on deflections) is wider than the whole effect of shear deformation in its tables (at most 1.3 % on a moment and 3.5 % on a deflection between the bracketed and unbracketed values), so these targets would also be met without shear deformation; and the shear stiffness is calibrated on a difference the source prints to one significant digit.
